lesson.child_mission: Energy changes (transforms) from one form to another in devices and living situations; we track what we can see, hear or feel.
lesson.evidence_instructions: Save the independent response, specific revisions and both short-answer explanations; record oral evidence for speaking tasks.
lesson.extension: Apply the same science idea to a new object or material, then compare two pieces of evidence for strength.
lesson.guided_practice:
PRACTISE BEFORE READING THE FEEDBACK
Describe the main energy change in a wind-up toy car releasing across the floor.

FEEDBACK
Stored/elastic or wound energy → movement (and some sound/heat).

WATCH FOR
Listing every possible tiny change without a main observable transfer overwhelms the model.
lesson.independent_task:
INDEPENDENT EVIDENCE
For six devices, name the starting form, ending form you detect and one wasted/extra form (e.g. heat).

Write a short reflection naming one observation or step you corrected and why.
lesson.learning_intention: Energy changes (transforms) from one form to another in devices and living situations; we track what we can see, hear or feel.
materials: Optional: safe everyday objects for observation
lesson.offline_alternative: Use paper and pencil to complete the original task, then retain a photograph or short parent observation as evidence.
lesson.parent_notes:
Parent: Marking guidance for the independent task: For six devices, name the starting form, ending form you detect and one wasted/extra form (e.g. heat). Accept equivalent original responses that show the same skill.

Parent: Written model 1: Sample: new object/context, two named observations, claim about transfer linked to that evidence.

Parent: Written model 2: Sample misconception: Listing every possible tiny change without a main observable transfer overwhelms the model.. Correction: Stored/elastic or wound energy → movement (and some sound/heat). with evidence.

Parent: Likely misconception: Listing every possible tiny change without a main observable transfer overwhelms the model. Keep sample answers out of the child role.

Parent: Short-answer focus 1: Investigate or describe a fresh example (not the worked objects) that uses transfer. Record evidence and explain how it supports your claim.

Parent: Short-answer focus 2: Name one science misconception about transfer, correct it with evidence, and say why the correction works.

Parent: Marking notes: Accept a new example with named observations and a claim–evidence link about transfer. Reject title-only labels with no observation. / Accept a misconception plus corrected claim and evidence reason for transfer. Reject wording changes that leave the same error..

teach_steps.explain:
Energy changes (transforms) from one form to another in devices and living situations; we track what we can see, hear or feel.

WHY IT MATTERS
This helps the learner base claims on observation, fair tests and design evidence, rather than guessing from a picture alone. Keep every claim linked to what was seen or measured.

HOW TO WORK
Read the worked example and name the observations, properties or test steps that carry the idea. Before looking at the correction, make your own attempt using the exact question provided. Compare your record with the feedback: did you use the same skill and show your evidence? If a result is uncertain, identify what would have to be observed or tested again. One deliberate, evidence-based revision is more useful than writing a longer answer.
